title: Add holistic cohorting and time-warp probing to improve regression sensitivity
author: Aisha Rahman
release_notes: Introduces cohort-based canary probing and a novel time-warp probe scheduler. Improves early detection of slow degradations in tail latency and throughput regressions; backwards compatible with existing canary configs.
description: Summary: This PR adds two coordinated features to the perf-canary stack: (1) a holistic cohorting service that groups traffic by behavioral fingerprints (payload size, sequence length, model variant, and feature flags) so canary probes exercise representative cohorts, and (2) a time-warp prober that synthesizes historical traffic slices at shifted time horizons (day-of-week / hour-of-day offsets) to surface regressions that only appear under certain temporal contexts. Motivation: We observed recurring regressions that escaped standard canary windows because they were conditioned on traffic cohorts or only appeared at specific daily patterns. By combining cohorted sampling with horizon-shifted probes, we increase sensitivity to slow, covariate-dependent degradations without increasing probe volume or false positives.

review_conversation: Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice isolation between cohorting and probing. Question: how do you avoid cohort starvation for low-volume customers?

Aisha Rahman (author): We add an entropy-based minimum probe allocation per cohort (configurable) and fall back to cross-cohort shadowing when volume is insufficient. Added notes in doc and default config.
Lina Chen (reviewer): The horizon aggregation looks promising; can you clarify how you handle seasonality vs drift? Could be high false positives during big traffic shifts.

Aisha Rahman (author): We combine horizon fusion with a seasonal baseline detector — a lightweight seasonal decomposition step (weekly/hourly) before changepoint scoring. This is in evaluator/horizon_aggregator.py and documented in the runbook.
Tomás Becker (reviewer): CI failing on test_timewarp - flakes in env setup. Can we stabilize before merge?
Aisha Rahman (author): Fixed by isolating the test port allocations and adding deterministic RNG seeds; reran CI.
ci_summary: Initial CI: 1 failing unit test (test_timewarp) due to port collision; fix applied in commit c7a4d10 and workflow matrix updated. Full integration matrix passed on rerun (linux/amd64 + linux/arm + integration). Performance gate: microbenchmarks show median probe runtime within 1.5x of baseline; resource request increased slightly to avoid scheduling jitter.
merge_outcome: merged via squash; merge commit message summarizes cohorter, timewarp prober, horizon aggregator. No manual revert required. Post-merge: enabled feature gate behind 'timewarp' flag and rolled out to staging cluster for 48h smoke tests.
operational_notes: Default config is conservative: timewarp window = {0, +1, -1} day offsets, cohort_min_probes = 10/day. Operators can tune cohort weight decay and horizon aggregation alpha. Added dashboard panels: 'Timewarp probe success rate', 'Cohort probe coverage', 'Horizon drift score'. Alerts: drift_score > 3 sigma for 15m triggers pager with auto-pause option. Runbook steps included in docs/perf-canary/timewarp.md.
testing_notes: Added synthetic scenarios: payload-shift, seq-length skew, feature-flag rollout. Unit tests validate deterministic fingerprinting and probe deterministic replay. Integration tests exercise end-to-end scoring with an injected regression and verify rollback guard triggers.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. All new features are opt-in via feature gates. CPU/GPU resource increase is limited to probe replicas; autoscaling thresholds added. Potential false positives mitigated by horizon-fusion consensus (requires >= 2 horizon signals to escalate).
how_to_validate: 1) Enable timewarp feature flag on staging. 2) Deploy prober with cohort_min_probes=5 and run the synthetic payload-shift scenario. 3) Confirm horizon drift score rises and canary orchestrator pauses rollout according to policy. 4) Check dashboards and logs for probe coverage per cohort.
notes_for_release: Ship behind feature flag. Recommend enabling in non-production first and observe for 72h before enabling in Dedicated clusters. Add to next SRE runbook rotation.
